scope: Bounded client release/reader/adapter/journal peer review plus actual local Chromium IndexedDB/Web Locks fault-injection checks. Submission lifecycle receives a separate peer review; generated bindings and contract source are not claimed as fully read here.

files.reviewedBoundary: Exact accessor-free bounded snapshots; trusted manifest/roster; pinned Testnet/RPC/protocol; actual DKG transcript signatures and auditor point; network/deployment/asset identity derivation; exact PoolConfig ScVal/XDR and branded immutable release.

Returned ledger key/type/storage/durability identity, Config and WASM bytes, bounded JSON and canonical XDR, record digest/profile/window, checkpoint history and final reread, cancellation and full-Fr revocation tag.
Public-only canonical157 fields,256-byte proof transport, exact addresses, bridge/fee presence, nonce offsets and generated ABI argument mapping. No proof acceptance in encoder.

Atomic pending records and exact source/NF/CM/record reservations; whole-store bounded consistency check; immutable terminal outcomes; explicit retry ancestry/no forks/cycles; actual two-page locking/races and corruption rejection. Final pending() uses the same complete audit before exposing only immutable pending hashes after reload.

Read current SDK XDR response fixtures and identity, DKG, checkpoint, missing/expired record, cancellation and actual13-revoke-envoy full-field regression assertions. Execution after correction reported by author, not rerun in this pass.

Author-owned independent browser harness: bundles exact reviewed source, actual two pages and IndexedDB/Web Locks, fault injection, explicit retry history and strict no-external/console/page/CSP evidence.

findings.problem: If the pending immutable attempt survived but its reservation rows were missing, conflicts/get/direct commit could accept apparently unreserved state. A different source and record could then create another pending attempt using the same nullifier. Normal atomic IDB writes should prevent partial crash commits; this was a corruption fail-closed omission, not evidence that IndexedDB broke atomicity.
findings.redEvidence: The preserved original source bundle passed12/17 expanded independent browser checks and failed missing-reservation conflicts/get/commit, extra reservation and lost-terminal checks.
findings.fix: A bounded whole-journal audit now validates all attempt/terminal/reservation relationships inside each transaction before reads/writes, with no truncation. Immutable terminal history and explicit known_not_sent retry ancestry are also validated.
findings.greenEvidence: Current exact source hash passed22/22 independent actual Chromium checks, including the five original failures and two-page explicit retry race. Final pending() reload discovery and corruption rejection both passed.

findings.problem: readRevocationAt previously required the full Poseidon revocation tag to be below2^128, although only its tree index uses low128 bits. Genuine generated revocation records were rejected.
findings.fix: Canonical field decoder retains Fr bound; reader now requires only nonzero full-field tag. Current test uses the actual13-revoke-envoy proof tag and archive root reconstruction.
findings.verificationBoundary: Author reported13/13 focused adapter+reader checks and typecheck passed after correction. This reviewer read the final source/test but did not rerun that suite; comprehensive parent gate supplies separate execution evidence.

limits: No external audit, no all-repository audit and no no-bugs guarantee. Runtime source was edited by its owner; this reviewer authored only the browser harness and review records.
Manifest and DKG roster are trusted release-channel inputs. The branded release is not evidence of deployment until the reader obtains matching code/config.
Reader authenticates configured network/contract/ABI identities against a trusted RPC. It does not verify SCP consensus or provide independent ledger-inclusion proofs.

Actual browser tests use public synthetic attempt data, real IndexedDB/Web Locks, two pages and reload. They do not test OS power loss, physical fsync guarantees, browser-process restart, quota exhaustion, multi-device conflict or hostile same-origin code.
Deliberate partial-store mutations are fault injection. Deletion/rollback of the entire browser profile can erase all local evidence and is not prevented by this journal.
Journal retains up to10000 attempts and60000 reservations; bounds fail rather than truncate. Large-history latency and real-phone memory/performance have not been benchmarked.

Unknown attempts retain reservations. Only separately authenticated terminal evidence or explicit known_not_sent retry logic can release/reuse state; browser storage alone does not establish chain success.
No live wallet signing, external RPC, transaction simulation/submission, deployment or real-funds operation was performed in this pass.

separateScope.note: Earlier source read by this reviewer was not used to claim current full-file coverage after lifecycle changes.
